title: Ivo and the Summit
premise: When a government survey team vanishes in the Karst Range, blacklisted mountain guide Rosalind Fairweather is the only person willing to lead a search upriver to the glacier's forbidden source. She and her estranged partner Ivo, now a park warden sworn to arrest her, discover the surveyors were mapping an illegal mining operation sanctioned from above — and that one surveyor survived, hiding in the ice caves with evidence that could ruin powerful men. As calving season threatens to seal the route forever, Rosalind must choose between destroying the evidence to protect her own anonymity and carrying it out to face justice, and Ivo must choose between his badge and the woman he loves. They bring the truth down the mountain together, at the cost of Ivo's career and Rosalind's invisibility, but the exposure of the mining ring clears her name.
about_author: Ines Montrose is the pen name of a former alpine rescue dispatcher who spent a decade listening to radio traffic from mountains she never climbed. She writes adventure fiction from a small farmhouse, where she keeps a wall of topographic maps annotated with stories that never made the official reports.

chapters.title: The Blacklist
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Working under a false name at a lowland outfitter, she learns a government survey team has gone missing in the Karst Range — territory she was banned from entering years ago after a client death she didn't cause. The beat: restless unease, the past circling back.

chapters.title: Gear With No Tracks
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Warden Ivo Voss inspects the abandoned survey camp: tents pitched neatly, food untouched, no footprints beyond the perimeter. His report is dismissed by superiors eager to close the file. Beat: professional dread hardening into private obsession.

chapters.title: An Old Debt
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A dying outfitter friend begs Rosalind to search for his granddaughter, Juniper, a junior surveyor on the lost team. Rosalind refuses — then finds Juniper's notebook left at her door. Beat: guilt tipping into resolve.

chapters.title: The Warden's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ordered to declare the area closed, Ivo instead quietly requests the old search files and finds Rosalind's name redacted throughout. He realizes the blacklist was engineered. Beat: loyalty to the service beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She slips onto the river alone at dawn, following it toward the forbidden source before calving season opens — and seals — the high route. Flashbacks reveal the client death that ruined her. Beat: grim freedom.

chapters.title: Two Banners
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Sent to intercept 'an unauthorized party on the river,' Ivo tracks Rosalind instead of arresting her, telling himself he needs information. Their first confrontation on a gravel bar ends in stalemate. Beat: duty and love pulling taut.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Whispers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Forced to travel together when a storm floods the lower trail, they navigate a slot gorge where the river vanishes underground. They find a surveyor's glove snagged on rebar — cut, not torn. Beat: wary truce, first real clue.

chapters.title: Juniper's Notebook
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The recovered pages show the team found something at the source: fresh blasting scars beneath the glacier, ore samples, and a final entry — 'they know we know.' Beat: fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Man Below
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In an ice cave near the source they find Emrys, the sole survivor, half-frozen, guarding a satchel of documents. He trusts neither of them and holds a knife on Rosalind until Ivo vouches with his warrant card. Beat: fragile alliance forged in cold.

chapters.title: What the Ice Remembers
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV (first time). He recounts the ambush: men with company radios, not criminal ones, executing the team and dumping gear to fake a wandering death. The documents name officials in both countries. Beat: horror transmuted into testimony.

chapters.title: The Descent That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Radio contact: a 'rescue' helicopter inbound — sent by the very people named in the satchel. They hide in the ice caves while searchers with rifles sweep the glacier above. Beat: claustrophobic terror, trust deepening between Rosalind and Ivo.

chapters.title: Calving Season Opens
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The glacier begins to calve; the route downstream will close within days. Emrys's frostbite worsens. They must move now or be entombed with the truth. Beat: the clock becomes the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Serac Field
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A brutal crossing through collapsing ice towers; Ivo saves Rosalind from a fall, and she saves Emrys, each act eroding old grievances. A serac collapse destroys their backtrack route. Beat: love rekindled under mortal pressure.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Moraine
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A 'friendly' ranger patrol finds them — Emrys recognizes one man from the ambush and bolts, forcing a firefight in which Ivo is wounded shielding him. They escape over the moraine as the patrol reports them as hostiles. Beat: paranoia justified, cost paid.

chapters.title: The Long Dark
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A night sheltering in a coal seam while Ivo's wound festers; Rosalind treats him with kit and confession, telling the full truth of the client death — a cover-up she stayed silent about to survive. Beat: raw honesty, forgiveness asked and given.

chapters.title: River of Ash
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Feverish, Ivo insists they follow the river's resurgence out of the range rather than any road. Rosalind carries him partway; Emrys navigates by the survey map. Beat: reversal of strength, tenderness without sentimentality.

chapters.title: The Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The valley mouth is sealed by company security posing as police. Rosalind splits the group: she'll draw them off with the decoy satchel while Ivo and Emrys take the documents through the gorge. Beat: sacrifice offered, refused, renegotiated.

chapters.title: The Run Downriver
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A raft chase through the gorge rapids, Rosalind baiting the pursuers while radioing false coordinates. She wrecks the raft and goes into the water. Beat: peak action, apparent loss.

chapters.title: What Ivo Carried Out
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Believing Rosalind drowned, Ivo delivers the documents to a federal prosecutor Emrys trusted — then learns the decoy satchel contained Rosalind's own exculpatory files from years ago. Beat: grief braided with dawning hope.

chapters.title: The Source Stands Open
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind survives downstream, half-drowned, and walks out to the checkpoint as arrests begin — the mining ring exposed overnight. She surrenders voluntarily, choosing justice over invisibility. Beat: courage completing its arc.

chapters.title: Hearings and High Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the inquiry, Emrys testifies, Ivo resigns his commission rather than perjure himself, and the blacklist is struck down. The two meet outside the courthouse as equals, unbadged and unhidden. Beat: vindication earned, not granted.

chapters.title: The River Again
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, closing. Spring: Rosalind and Ivo guide a memorial climb for the lost survey team, scattering their effects at the source, which calving season has finally opened to daylight. Beat: peace hard-won; the wilderness forgives nothing, but people can.
